name: Show the reach instead of claiming it
problem: A plain grid of projects can't tell a visitor that 5 TEN builds installations from New York to Las Vegas.
fix: A 3D globe pins every installation where it was built. Spin it, tap a pin, and the photo and case study pop up.
result: Visitors understand the studio's reach in seconds, before they read a word.
engineer: Pins are read from the Projects collection through data attributes. Invisible hitboxes handle hover and tap, and nearby pins group into clusters.

name: Add a project once and it shows up everywhere
problem: Without a system, adding new work means editing several pages by hand, and older projects clutter the portfolio.
fix: The team adds a project in the Webflow CMS with its location. It lands on the globe, the Projects grid and its own page. A "Has case study" switch keeps older work on the globe only.
result: New work goes live in minutes, without a developer.
engineer: Webflow can't bind a switch to an attribute, so the globe reads two filtered Collection Lists and the grid filters to case studies only.

name: Let the videos do the selling
problem: Installation videos are the studio's strongest proof, but small embeds don't show the scale.
fix: A pinned gallery holds the page still while the videos play full-screen, then lets go the moment it ends.
result: Every visitor sees the work at full size, and scrolling never gets stuck.
engineer: The scroll distance lives on one runway element, calibrated per breakpoint (160 / 150 / 135 / 120vh). A parent's overflow: hidden was silently killing sticky, so it became overflow: clip.

name: Big visuals that still load fast on a phone
problem: 3D and WebGL can make a phone page slow and drain the battery.
fix: 3D only runs while it's on screen. On phones the rotating process shapes swap to lightweight drawings.
result: The same wow on desktop and a quick page on mobile.
engineer: An IntersectionObserver starts and stops each render loop. A bug that started the loop twice was removed, which halved the CPU cost. Below the mobile breakpoint a 150px SVG replaces the canvas.

name: Explain a technical process without a wall of text
problem: Consulting, engineering and execution is hard to picture from paragraphs, and prospects arrived with the same questions.
fix: Each step gets its own rotating wireframe shape and one short line of copy.
result: Prospects understand how 5 TEN works before the first call.
engineer: Wireframe platonic solids in Three.js. Page CSS was trimmed from 16 sections to 8 to stay under Webflow's silent page-CSS limit.

name: Prove "we serve families nationwide"
problem: Every firm says it serves clients everywhere. A sentence doesn't build trust.
fix: A live map shows real case wins across the country. Filter by case type, hover a pin for a summary, click it for the whole story.
result: Visitors see the evidence in seconds and trust the firm before they call.
engineer: A D3 projection over us-atlas TopoJSON. The nation is drawn once to a hidden canvas and each dot reads one pixel, replacing about 22,000 geometry checks with a ~7ms pass. Popups float in a fixed layer so the map's clipping can't cut them off.

name: A new case win becomes a new pin
problem: Hard-coded results would go stale the moment the firm won another case.
fix: Staff add a case in the CMS (type, state, outcome) and a pin appears on the homepage map and the results page.
result: The proof grows with every case, with no developer involved.
engineer: Pins come from a hidden Collection List through data attributes. Nearby pins cluster automatically.

name: Spanish-speaking families feel at home
problem: Many of the firm's clients speak Spanish first, and most law-firm sites treat Spanish as an afterthought.
fix: The whole site works in English and Spanish. One toggle switches it and remembers the choice.
result: Families can read about their case in the language they think in.
engineer: Copy ships in both languages and a toggle swaps it in place, saving the choice for the next visit.

name: Show up for the questions clients actually ask
problem: Standalone articles don't add up. Search engines and AI assistants couldn't see what the firm knows.
fix: A connected content system links a 58-term vocabulary, practice-area pages and articles to each other. Adding a term links it everywhere.
result: A visitor can go from a question to the right practice area to a consultation, and the firm reads as an authority to search and AI.
engineer: Topics, Insights and Practice Areas are cross-referenced collections, and the category and vocabulary hubs are generated from the same references.

name: Updates ship without breaking the site
problem: The site outgrew Webflow's code limits, and fixes sometimes didn't show up after publishing.
fix: Styles ship from pinned, versioned files that are checked live before they switch.
result: The firm never sees a half-updated page, and every change can be rolled back.
engineer: Five page stylesheets load from GitHub through a CDN, each pinned to an exact commit so caches can't serve stale code. Rolling back is a one-line pin change.
snippet:
<!-- each page head holds one pinned line; a change ships by moving the pin -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="…/homepage.css@37f5238">
<!-- rollback = re-pin the previous commit -->

name: One mark from favicon to billboard
problem: A logo that only looks right large falls apart in a browser tab or a social avatar.
fix: The mark has a size-specific favicon with a thicker stroke, drawn to the pixel grid.
result: The brand stays recognisable at 16px and at wall size.
engineer: At 16px the square merged into the ring, so the small version enlarges the square and snaps strokes to whole pixels.

name: Visitors always know where to click
problem: When accents are used everywhere, nothing stands out as the next step.
fix: Orange is reserved for actions and highlights. The Figma-style selection UI gets its own blue.
result: Every orange element is something you can do, so the path to contact is obvious.
engineer: Signal orange is a single token. Decorative states use separate tokens, so accent creep can't happen by accident.

name: Readable for everyone
problem: White text on the orange accent measured under 3 : 1 contrast, which is hard to read for many people.
fix: Text on the accent is always the near-black Void colour.
result: Buttons clear 7 : 1 contrast, well past accessibility guidelines.
engineer: Checked against WCAG 2.2 AA and AAA. The on-accent text colour is a token, so every new button inherits it.
snippet:
:root { --on-signal: #07080D; }   /* 7 : 1 on the accent */
.btn-primary { background: var(--signal); color: var(--on-signal); }

name: One system for every surface
problem: Without rules, every new page or asset would drift a little further from the brand.
fix: Six colour tokens, one type scale and a construction grid define the whole identity.
result: Each new page, card or deck looks like it belongs, without starting from scratch.
engineer: Tokens map one-to-one to Webflow variables, so a colour change in one place updates the whole site.
